claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On three dual-arm manipulation tasks, the authors report that their trajectory-refined GLIDE guardrails raise teleoperation success from 0/10, 1/10 and 0/10 under unguarded OpenTV to 7/10, 9/10 and 9/10, respectively; a domain-expert hardcoded guardrail baseline reaches 2/10, 6/10 and 6/10.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For success-only-trained policies, runtime guardrails raise tomato-transfer success from 0% to 60% and marker-handover success from 20% to 50% in 10 trials per condition, while wine-serving success falls from 50% to 40%. With mixed-quality GLIDE data and the guardrail active, success is 70%, 60% and 60% across the three tasks.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The small task suite and 10-trial conditions do not establish broad task generalization, robust safety guarantees, or superior performance across robot platforms and longer-horizon tasks.

evidence_gaps.description: The authors now provide a public real-robot runtime repository and demonstration datasets. Neither was downloaded or executed in this review, and no independent reproduction or larger-trial evaluation of the reported effects was performed.
Task, robot and sensing coverage are narrow; runtime filtering is proprioceptive and transfer to longer-horizon or mobile tasks is untested.

record.importance_rationale: If the approach holds across tasks and larger trials, generated execution-time constraints could make imperfect teleoperation data more useful and allow learned policies to benefit from it without removing runtime protection. Score 5 reflects a meaningful robotics data and control result; evidence is limited to three tasks and 10-trial conditions in one author study.
limitations: All results are reported by the authors and were not independently reproduced.
Each reported condition uses 10 evaluation trials, so estimates are coarse and uncertainty intervals are not supplied in the inspected text.
The study covers three manipulation tasks on one robot setup; long-horizon and mobile manipulation remain future work.
Runtime guardrails use proprioception only; vision and tactile runtime filtering are identified as future extensions.
Runtime guardrails do not improve every task: reported wine-serving success decreases from 50% to 40% for one success-only policy condition.
The authors provide public runtime code and demonstration datasets, but this activation did not download, execute or independently validate them.
record.summary: GLIDE is a framework that generates executable command guardrails from task descriptions, refines them using teleoperation trajectories and reuses them during policy execution. Across three dual-arm manipulation tasks, the authors report that GLIDE guardrails raise teleoperation success to 70%, 90% and 90%, compared with 0%, 10% and 0% under unguarded teleoperation and 20%, 60% and 60% under domain-expert hardcoded guardrails. In 10-trial policy conditions, runtime guardrails improve two success-only-trained tasks but reduce wine-serving success from 50% to 40%; mixed-quality GLIDE data with filtering reaches 70%, 60% and 60%. The paper reports a bounded physical-robot study, not general safety or broad task transfer. The authors provide a public runtime repository and demonstration datasets, which were not independently run or analyzed here.

technical.claimed_result: With learned guardrails, teleoperation success is reported as 70%, 90% and 90% across tomato-plate transfer, marker handover and wine serving, versus 0%, 10% and 0% unguarded and 20%, 60% and 60% with domain-expert guardrails. In 10-trial policy tests, runtime filtering changes success-only policy success from 0% to 60% and 20% to 50% on two tasks, but from 50% to 40% on wine serving.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible preprint reports the three task tables, trajectory-refinement process and runtime filtering comparisons. All results are author-reported; no independent reproduction was performed.
technical.implementation_status: Research prototype evaluated on a physical dual-arm manipulation setup; broad platform deployment is not established.
technical.mechanism: A coding agent infers failure points from task descriptions, generates executable filters on proposed arm commands, records guarded teleoperation outcomes, diagnoses failures from video and trajectories, refines the filters, and applies the final guardrails to both data collection and learned-policy execution.
technical.regime: Three dual-arm manipulation tasks: tomato plate transfer, marker handover and standing, and wine serving. Each data-collection baseline/round and policy condition reports 10 trials. Policy experiments use pi_0.5 trained on success-only or mixed GLIDE data, or unguarded OpenTV data. Runtime filters use proprioception.
technical.reproducibility: The preprint, author-linked project page, runtime repository and dataset card are accessible. The code and data were not downloaded or run; independent reproduction and larger trial counts remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: Domain-expert hardcoded guardrails during collection and matched guarded/unguarded execution of the same policy for deployment comparisons.

record.title: GLIDE reports that executable guardrails improve manipulation demonstrations and selected robot-policy trials
record.why_it_matters: Robotic demonstrations can fail when teleoperation cannot keep objects stable or complete delicate handoffs. GLIDE tests a concrete mechanism: generate task-specific command filters, refine them from trajectory outcomes, and keep the filter active when policies learn from the resulting data. Its reported gains are promising but task-specific, with only 10 policy trials per condition and an exception where runtime filtering lowers success.
